source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: Ultrasound waves (FF = 1.1 MHz, PRF = 1000 Hz, TBD = 0.5 ms, SD = 1 s, ISI = 1 s, and DC = 50%) were delivered into the dorsal raphe nucleus (DRN) for 30 min per day for 2 weeks.

flags.reason: Seventy mice were used overall, but ultrasound was actually delivered to several different, only partly overlapping cohorts (11 CRS+TUS for behaviour, 3 DRN+TUS for c-Fos immunofluorescence, 5 CRS+TUS for LC-MS, 3 for HE staining); no single total exposed to ultrasound is stated.
Text states TUS was delivered '30 min per day for 2 weeks', implying about 14 daily sessions, but an explicit session count is never given.
Depressive mice were 'redivided into CRS + Sham and CRS + TUS groups according to the SPI' (matched on sucrose preference index), not by simple randomisation.
Only c-Fos cell counting is described as done by 'double-blind observers'; blinding of TUS/Sham delivery itself is not described.

readout_other: Sucrose preference test; tail suspension test; c-Fos immunofluorescence; LC-MS quantification of serotonin (5-HT); H&E histology
direction_notes: DRN-TUS increased c-Fos-positive neuron counts and serotonin concentration in the DRN, and improved depression-like behaviours (increased sucrose preference index, decreased tail-suspension immobility) relative to sham in chronic-restraint-stress mice.
safety_notes: HE staining showed no tissue hemorrhage or damage in the DRN after 2 weeks of TUS; the estimated maximum temperature rise during 30 min of stimulation was about 0.02 °C.

exposures.label: Dorsal raphe nucleus (DRN-TUS) in chronic-restraint-stress depression model

device.model: head-mounted miniature power ultrasonic transducer (custom-built, PZT-4/epoxy 1-3 composite)

timing.protocol_description: 1-s sonication trains with a 1-s inter-stimulus interval, delivered for 30 min per day for 2 weeks to the DRN of freely behaving mice; the CRS+Sham group had the transducer output switched off.
